notes: LAMPOST (Light A' Multilayer Periodic Optical SNSPD Target) is a proof-of-concept optical haloscope experiment searching for dark photon dark matter via coherent absorption in a multilayer dielectric stack. The paper reports the first experimental constraints on dark photon DM in the 0.7–0.8 eV mass range with kinetic mixing ϵ ≳ 10^−12, improving existing limits by up to a factor of two. The experiment used 180 hours of data collection with superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) achieving a dark count rate of ~6×10^−6 counts/s. The primary SNSPD registered 4 counts and the reference SNSPD registered 5 counts. A 90% confidence limit was derived using a Poisson statistical treatment that marginalizes over the unknown dark count rate. The local DM density assumed is ρ_DM ≃ 0.4 GeV/cm³ with a standard truncated Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity distribution. The data point represents a mass-independent (flat) bound across the 0.7–0.8 eV range; the limit ϵ ≳ 10^−12 applies throughout this mass interval.
